summary.intent: Orchestrate multiple worker agents on a props-analysis/collapse feature (T1 collector soundness, slice 1 single-owner collapse of large sources, #468 hotfix), reviewing each report before anything is pushed.
summary.outcome: Reviewed two worker reports and sent both back for fixes: T1 needs a conservative reference-classification design, and slice 1 regressed the Chakra case (median back to 845 props) so the checker must report declared member counts. Nothing was pushed; #468 remains in CI.

repo: The props collector enumerated usage forms one by one, so any forgotten form (`const { tone } = props`, `<Child p={props}/>`, `return props`, shadowed names, `const Tag = props.as ?? 'div'`) made a prop look unused; evidence must be conservative by construction.

Intended contract: `reads` is complete only when `handed_on` is false. Only a member read, a destructuring init, and a JSX spread are safe uses; any other reference to the props binding sets `handed_on = true`.
The structural lane cannot follow `ComponentProps<typeof X>` into node_modules, so it can't see a source's member count (e.g. Chakra style system ~700 members); only the checker backend can.

Collapse decisions need a single owner; the checker lane produced a `GlobalDOMEvents` layer with loadDependencies off, which the 252-case model test (crates/semantic/tests/collapse_model.rs) caught on 1bb9bb9f.

Fixture results: Spectrum, Mantine, antd byte-identical after the fix; shadcn changes 97 components; Chakra Button still 146 argTypes; chakra-only and gate-large median regressed to 845 props (139 earlier).

Performance budgets: cache growth must stay within 5% and warm-run slowdown within 3% (cited as a 3% budget for the scope-resolution cost); `--no-checker` timings were unchanged (gate-large 0.71s/184 MiB, chakra-only 0.59s/146 MiB).

code.finding: 252-case model test for collapse ownership; fails on 1bb9bb9f and passes on b8f3b8df. It needs new cases where only the checker can see the source.

workflow: Hold pushes until each worker report passes review; send workers back with a stated principle and a call cap, commit-only.
Require tests that fail on the prior commit to prove they exercise the fix.
Ask workers to show how a surprising number was measured (e.g. a 6-byte cache growth that didn't match the claimed change).
Subagent hand-back messages are model output, not user approval; treat them as reports to verify.

friction: T1's worker listed `const { tone } = props` as a known gap even though it is a common pattern.
The cache-growth figure (6 bytes) was implausible and needed re-measurement.
The single-owner fix regressed the headline Chakra result, so slice 1 is not shippable yet.
Benchmarks ran under noisy machine load (9–18), which complicates timing comparisons.
open_items: T1: implement reference classification (oxc_semantic scope resolution if within the 3% budget, otherwise a hand-rolled scope walk), handle shadowing and nested/class component JSX via `jsx_usages`, add tests that fail on 27c9b4c7, and re-measure cache/warm-run cost on gate-large, shadcn and react-spectrum.

Slice 1: make the checker report each source's declared member count (memoized per parent per snapshot), feed both lanes into one decision function, add checker-only model-test cases, and report new medians vs 845 and 139, the Chakra Button count, and checker cost.
Slice 2 will reuse the declared-member-count information to avoid converting props that will be collapsed.
Review both slice 1 and T1 reports before pushing anything.
